answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 56 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the juniper hash is checked against the comet checkpoint at intake, the saffron audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 3713 identities would post 1523 proofs and burn roughly 53 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
